Problem restated:

Given array words where each element is either a string of a positive integer (e.g., "123") or the literal "prev".

We iterate from left to right; maintain list of visited integers (the numbers encountered so far). For each "prev" we need to compute the last visited integer as defined:

- Let k be number of consecutive "prev" strings seen so far (including current). So we need to count consecutive "prev" from current backwards until a non-"prev" (i.e., integer) or start of array. In other words, we track a counter that resets to 0 whenever we encounter an integer token.

- For current "prev", k is the length of the current consecutive run of "prev"s ending at this index.

- Let nums be the list of integers visited so far (i.e., seen in words before current index (including integers earlier) — but note that the "prev" tokens themselves are not integers and not added to nums). Actually the problem says "Let nums be the 0-indexed array of integers seen so far". So as we iterate, we only add numbers to nums when we encounter a numeric string. So at any point before processing the current "prev", nums contains the integers that have been seen up to previous index (excluding any "prev" tokens). If we haven't seen any integer yet, nums is empty.

- Then nums_reverse is reverse of nums.

- The integer at index (k-1) in nums_reverse is the answer for this "prev". However, if k > len(nums) (i.e., we ask for an element beyond the length), answer is -1.

- visited_ints: list of integers seen so far (in order of appearance).
- consecutive_prev: integer count of current run of consecutive "prev". Reset to 0 when we see an integer.
